messages:
Riley (AE): Heads-up — ZenithHealth signed off on a 2-node on-prem POC. They want a short install + validation (2 GPU workers, 1 control plane) next week and automatic fallback to our hosted API if private path flaps. Need a tight preflight checklist we can send their infra and security teams.
Tess (SE): I'll draft the checklist. Quick: will they let us create the operator SA or will they hand over a kubeconfig for bootstrap?
Riley (AE): They said infra prefers to create creds, but security may require a short-lived kubeconfig for convenience.
Marco (Field Eng): For HW/drivers: recommend Linux kernel >=5.15, NVIDIA driver >=525.x for H100/A100 compatibility, CUDA >=12.1. Ask them to paste `nvidia-smi -L` and `nvidia-smi -q` outputs. Confirm NVLINK/IB if multi-GPU.
Ellen (Security): From Sec: no long-lived kubeconfigs. If they provide a kubeconfig it must have an expiration <=24h and IP allowlist. Preferred: they create a namespaced ServiceAccount with minimal RBAC and give us the token + RBAC YAML. Explicit: no cluster-admin. Also need a short note on cert/key custody (KMS/HSM?) and rotation cadence.
Jules (SRE): Network: allow outbound to registry.redwood.ai:443, DNS (udp/53), NTP (udp/123), and our fallback API hostnames on 443. If airgapped, we need image tarballs + signed manifest. Confirm MTU >= 1400 and whether HTTPS pulls go via an internal proxy.
Marco (Field Eng): Put these quick verification commands in the email (copy/paste):
```
# on each worker node
nvidia-smi -L
nvidia-smi -q | head -n 80
uname -r
cat /etc/os-release
# control plane checks
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl version --short
# container runtime
crictl --version || docker --version
# kernel logs (driver issues)
dmesg | tail -n 200
```
Tess (SE): I'll include a minimal RBAC snippet they can apply if they create the SA. Also an alternative bootstrap flow where they hand a 24h kubeconfig with IP allowlist.
Ellen (Security): Also request: who manages node patching? What's the vulnerability/patch cadence? If SELinux/AppArmor are enforced, list profiles. Where do they store node private keys? KMS vendor + key IDs preferred.
Jules (SRE): For observability: ask them to forward node syslogs temporarily or allow us to run a read-only sidecar to collect driver logs. We also need access to pull pod logs during the POC.
Marco (Field Eng): Optional stress test: we'll provide a tiny 2-worker container image and a `docker run`/`ctr` snippet to exercise CUDA allocations. Ask them to run it and watch `dmesg` for GPU resets/OOMs.
Tess (SE): RBAC snippet (apply if they create SA):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: redwood-operator-sa
  namespace: redwood-system
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: redwood-operator-role
  namespace: redwood-system
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","secrets","configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch","create","update","patch","delete"]
---
kind: RoleBinding
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: redwood-operator-binding
  namespace: redwood-system
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: redwood-operator-sa
  namespace: redwood-system
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: redwood-operator-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
Riley (AE): We'll also include pricing for spinning a short Dedicated pool vs using hosted fallback (metered). They asked for ballpark numbers.
Ellen (Security): If they insist we bring a kubeconfig, require: expiration <=24h, source IP allowlist, and scoped RBAC. No privileged tokens and no persistent credentials stored on our side.
Tess (SE): I'll prepare the one-pager: checklist, copy/paste commands, RBAC YAML, airgap import steps, and fallback API key plan.
installer-bot: apiKey:create requested by Tess (SE) -> created scoped key: zenith-poc-fallback (inference-only) expires=14d
Jules (SRE): I'll join the kickoff for the first 20m (network/airgap/MTU/logging). Marco will take driver/debug and the stress test.
Marco (Field Eng): I'll bring the stress test commands and logging tips.
Ellen (Security): I'll join to confirm RBAC and KMS expectations.
Riley (AE): Thanks team — I'll send the buyer email with the one-pager and ask for outputs (nvidia-smi, kubectl, dmesg) by EOD tomorrow. :rocket:
